title: evaluator_attestation correctness verdict (v1)
description: Cross-repo contract for s3://alpha-engine-research/backtest/{run_date}/evaluator_attestation.json — the sf-pipeline-policy.md §2.3a correctness verdict of the Evaluator stage (SF states EvaluatorDiagnostics + EvaluatorOptimize, crucible-backtester evaluate.py). Produced by crucible-backtester analysis/evaluator_attestation.py::build_stage_attestation on every uploading run; consumed by crucible-evaluator grading/attestation.py, which folds it into report_card['attestation'] and the Backtester/Research tiles. The verdict is the WORST of this stage's own ranking-metric battery (IC / hit rate / calibration, known-answer, run through the production functions on the wheels the spot box resolved) and the simulation engine's verdict at backtest/{run_date}/attestation.json. ABSENCE OF THIS OBJECT IS NOT A PASS: a consumer that cannot read it must resolve to UNKNOWN and withhold the correctness guarantee — that is the whole point of the artifact, and reading a missing verdict as 'older artifact, proceed' reproduces exactly the blindness §2.3a exists to remove. A body stamped with a run_date other than the one requested is likewise UNKNOWN — a verdict from another cycle is never inherited. Additive-only evolution: new fields and new check names may be added; existing fields are never renamed or removed without a schema bump coordinated with the crucible-evaluator consumer.

schema.description: Frozen schema identifier. A consumer that does not recognise this string must resolve to UNKNOWN rather than best-effort parsing an artifact whose meaning it cannot establish.

component.description: The stage this verdict is about. Distinguishes this artifact from the sibling backtest/{run_date}/attestation.json, whose component is 'backtester'.

run_date.description: The NYSE trading day this cycle graded, matching the prefix the object is written under. A consumer MUST compare this against the run_date it asked for and resolve to UNKNOWN on a mismatch.

verdict.description: The combined §2.3a verdict: worst of `own.verdict` and `upstream.verdict`. Any FAIL wins; otherwise any non-PASS yields UNKNOWN; only both PASS yields PASS. FAIL means a known-answer check DISAGREED with its hand-derived expectation — evidence the numbers are wrong. UNKNOWN means a check, or the upstream read, could not RUN — absence of evidence. Both withhold the guarantee, but only FAIL accuses the arithmetic; collapsing them would make a broken venv read as a correctness regression. ONLY the literal 'PASS' grants the guarantee.

promotion_withheld.description: True whenever `verdict` is not PASS. When true the Evaluator stage ran under a forced --freeze: every diagnostic and artifact still landed, but config/executor_params.json, the other auto-apply configs and config/producer_champion.json were NOT promoted. This is the fail-closed action, recorded so a week with no promotion is distinguishable from a week with nothing to promote.

own.description: This stage's own known-answer battery over the ranking metrics it grades on: Spearman information coefficient, hit-rate/accuracy including the unresolved-outcome exclusion, and ECE/Brier calibration. Each check drives the production function and compares against a value derived from the metric's definition on paper.

engine.description: Versions of the interpreter and numeric stack that were attested. A verdict that does not identify the build it graded cannot explain a later divergence.

checks.description: One record per known-answer check. `expected` and `observed` are both carried — rather than a bare boolean — so a divergence is diagnosable from the artifact alone, without rerunning anything.

upstream.description: The simulation engine's verdict as this stage read it. Present with verdict=UNKNOWN and a populated `reason` when the object was absent, unreadable, stamped with another run_date, or carried an unrecognised verdict string.

reason.description: Why the verdict is what it is. On UNKNOWN this names which failure path was taken — absent object, unparseable body, run_date mismatch, unrecognised verdict string — so 'could not measure' is never confused with 'found a defect'.

as_of.description: S3 LastModified of the upstream verdict object, UTC ISO-8601. Null when the object could not be read. Surfaces on the console beside the state so a stale verdict reads stale rather than green.
